Geometric symmetry optimization of thermodynamic cycles with real fluids based on enthalpy decomposition
abstract: Symmetry principles offer a novel geometric perspective on thermodynamic cycles but face challenges with real fluid non-ideality. A Lie group decomposition approach, h=f(p)g(s) (where h, p, s denote specific enthalpy, pressure, and entropy), is proposed to transform thermodynamic optimization into a geometric topology problem. Coupled with Nash equilibrium analysis and validated by NIST property data, a ‘Skeleton + Correction’ geometric enthalpy expression model is constructed for H2O and CO2, with a relative error of less than 4%. Our findings indicate a robust geometric-physical correspondence in gas and gas-like regions, while in deep supercritical regimes, the correction part induces a measurable symmetry breaking. Based on the binary decomposition expression of enthalpy, a "C-P" diagram for the real-gases Brayton cycle is proposed. The thermodynamic parameters corresponding to the maximum work output are geometrically derived, revealing that the optimal state perfectly corresponds to the Nash equilibrium between the symmetry gain of the ideal skeleton and the energy penalty of the non-ideal correction. Furthermore, a comparative analysis reveals that the calculation error between the ideal gas model and the real gas model, which is roughly 20% for cases away from near-saturation region, can surge to over 500% near the mathematical singularities in numerical optimization, confirming the necessity of adopting the proposed real gas framework. Finally, a general semi-empirical expression for the optimal pressure ratio of the real-gas Brayton cycle is provided. This proposed frame work exhibits strong universality and can be extended to the symmetry optimization analysis of other thermodynamic cycles and working fluids.

Distributed solar generation forecasting using attention-based deep neural networks for cloud movement prediction
abstract: Accurate forecasts of distributed solar generation are necessary to maintain grid stability amid the increased uptake of distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, the high variability of solar generation over short time intervals (seconds to minutes) caused by cloud movement makes this forecasting task difficult. To address this, using cloud images, which capture the second-to-second changes in cloud cover affecting solar generation, has shown promise. Recently, deep neural networks with attention that focus on important regions of an image have been applied with success in many computer vision applications. However, whether such methods provide meaningful benefits for cloud movement forecasting, and how such improvements propagate through to downstream solar generation forecasting accuracy, remains under-explored. In this study, we conduct a large-scale empirical investigation of the impact of attention-based cloud forecasting on solar generation forecasting, addressing a gap that has been overlooked in the literature. To this end, we develop a pipeline that incorporates an attention-enhanced convolutional long short-term memory network and an existing self-attention-based video prediction method to forecast cloud movement using satellite imagery. The effectiveness of the resulting cloud forecasts is evaluated through their downstream impact on solar forecasting across 50 PV sites in Australia. We further provide insights into the cloud conditions under which attention-based cloud forecasting methods yield the most significant improvements in downstream solar forecasting accuracy. We find that for clouds at high altitudes, the cloud predictions obtained using attention-based methods result in solar forecast skill score improvements of 5.86% or more compared to non-attention-based methods.

abstract: Internal combustion engines are an important power source in the transportation sector, and recovering their waste heat is an effective approach to improving energy utilization and reducing fuel consumption. In this study, a vehicle-oriented, low-temperature evaporative, single-loop organic Rankine cycle (ORC) waste-heat recovery system was designed and built, enabling simultaneous and efficient recovery of waste heat from engine exhaust gas and jacket water. Based on prototype experiments, the effects of key operating parameters were investigated, and system performance tests as well as comparative tests of start–stop strategies were carried out over a wide range of engine operating conditions. The results indicate that the ORC system features an optimal turbine inlet temperature. When the cooling-water temperature varies within 15–25 °C, the fluctuation in generated power is less than 2 kW. Over the broad tested engine operating map, 77.8% of the operating points achieved an engine brake thermal efficiency (BTE) improvement of more than 3%. In addition, different start–stop strategies were experimentally compared and assessed in terms of warm-up time and operational safety. Practical operational recommendations suitable for vehicle applications are proposed, providing valuable references for real-world implementation.

Multi-modal photovoltaic anomaly detection via synergistic graph-contrastive regularization
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) anomaly detection is crucial for the effective operation and maintenance of PV systems. Although anomaly detection based on computer vision offers a promising solution, existing methods that rely on a single modality of images still have inherent limitations in practical scenarios. This study introduces a new comprehensive multi-modal dataset named PV-VISIR, which contains 9 categories and a total of 2146 pairs of labeled visible light and infrared images. Based on this dataset, a novel dualbranch multi-modal fusion framework is proposed to achieve more accurate anomaly detection. Experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in detection performance, achieving an mAP@0.5 of 0.781, which is 9.8% higher than the YOLOv8 baseline. The performance improvement can be largely attributed to two proposed modules, namely Label-driven Cross-Modal Registration (LCMR) and Synergistic Training via Prototypical Graph-Contrastive Regularization, which contribute 5.3% and 2.7% to the overall gain in mAP@0.5, respectively. The developed PV-VISIR dataset and the proposed framework are expected to jointly drive innovation in related methodologies and advance the development of PV monitoring technology.

abstract: In the context of carbon neutrality, enhancing energy efficiency in residential buildings is pivotal for achieving emission reduction targets. Although improving thermal insulation effectively reduces thermal loads, the performance of Air Source Heat Pumps (ASHPs) often degrades under low-load conditions. While conventional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) can optimize equipment operation, its reliance on pre-defined and static reward functions makes it difficult to adapt to the dynamic and subjective comfort preferences of occupants. To address this limitation, this study proposes a preference-conditioned DRL framework for adaptive HVAC control and implements a large-language-model-based natural language interface for preference input. The framework translates short occupant feedback into explicit preference constraints, enabling flexible and personalized adjustment of comfort–energy trade-offs. To verify the practical feasibility of the proposed method, a hardware integration platform based on Raspberry Pi was developed and deployed in a real-world residential setting. In the field tests, the proposed system achieved a 21% reduction in daily energy consumption under fixed-preference control and a 14% reduction under time-varying preference control compared with the corresponding baseline methods, while maintaining personalized occupant comfort. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive preference-aware HVAC control for improving residential energy efficiency while supporting personalized comfort requirements.

abstract: An integrated system utilizing potential from wind energy and anaerobic digestion is developed for the simultaneous production of electricity, methane, ammonia, and carbon dioxide. A dual CO 2 capture strategy based on liquefaction and calcium looping enables efficient carbon recovery in both storable and utilizable forms. The main novelty is the synergistic integration of these complementary capture pathways within one wind–biomass framework, enabling carbon recovery, utilization, and storage. The system is further assessed using 8784 h of NASA MERRA-2 hourly wind data to evaluate wind-intermittency effects beyond a steady-state assumption. A comprehensive 4E analysis (energy, exergy, economic, and environmental) is conducted. Under baseline conditions, the system achieves an exergy efficiency of 37.47%, net power output of 4358 kW, and a specific product cost of 38.37 $/GJ, with an avoided CO 2 -based environmental index of 0.5654 kg CO 2 /kWh. Production rates include 0.09296 kg/s liquid CO 2 , 0.7223 kg/s gaseous CO 2 , 0.01323 kg/s methane, and 0.00907 kg/s ammonia. The wind turbine shows the highest exergy destruction, while calcium looping dominates system cost. The payback period is estimated at 6.47 years. Across the scenario-specific selected optima, optimization increases exergy efficiency up to 47% and net power output up to 4744 kW, the avoided CO 2 -based environmental index up to 0.5998 kg CO 2 /kWh, liquid CO 2 (up to 0.1301 kg/s), gaseous CO 2 (up to 0.7249 kg/s), and ammonia production (up to 0.0262 kg/s), while reducing total specific product cost down to 35.96 $/GJ.

abstract: : Urban building energy demand under heatwaves is a rising concern, which is affected by local climate conditions. This study examines how extreme heatwaves and urban–rural climate differences affect cooling energy demand in public rental housing (PRH) in Hong Kong during 2022–2024. Four typical PRH sites were selected, three on the Kowloon Peninsula and one on a built-up island, and analyzed using building energy modeling driven by locally measured urban weather data and reference rural site weather data. Weather data indicate that urban–rural air and dew point temperature differences intensify during extreme heatwave (EH) versus normal summer (NS) days. The urban-rural difference in daily accumulated total cooling load intensity ( CL tot ) varies by urban site location, ranging from 3.8% lower to 4.0% higher in urban sites than the rural reference sites in EH days. A diurnal pattern is observed: At night (23:00 to 06:00), the accumulative total cooling load intensity is mostly higher than that from the reference rural site, reaching up to 17.4% higher in EH days and 24.3% higher in NS days. During the remainder of the day (07:00–22:00), the urban site generally results in a lower total cooling load intensity, up to 7.4% lower in EH days and 6.5% lower in NS days, than that from the reference rural site. Sensible cooling load is primarily associated with air temperature, whereas latent cooling load exhibits location-dependent responses to dew point temperature.

Parametric study of the techno-economic performance of Solar-MGT systems
abstract: Solar-assisted micro gas turbine (Solar-MGT) systems offer a promising solution for decentralised power generation by combining the reliability of gas turbines with the fuel-saving benefits of solar thermal input. This study presents a comprehensive techno-economic assessment of a Solar-MGT configuration using a detailed off-design model validated against both laboratory microturbine experiments and solar-assisted operation. A full-year simulation based on real meteorological data for Pretoria, South Africa captures the coupled effects of ambient conditions, receiver behaviour, Thermal Energy Storage (TES) operation, and component off-design performance within a unified framework. A refined component-level cost model is integrated into the analysis, enabling the influence of key subsystem characteristics on overall economic performance to be quantified. An extensive parametric study evaluates the impact of turbine inlet temperature, dish area, TES mass and charging temperature, recuperator effectiveness, and system mass flow rate. When parameter variations are normalised to represent similar increases in capital expenditure, the resulting designs span fuel-to-electric efficiencies of about 14–30% and levelised costs of electricity in the range 0.4–0.8 €/kWh. Upgrades focused on turbomachinery efficiency or recuperator effectiveness deliver the lowest costs of electricity (down to ≈0.4–0.76 €/kWh), albeit with a modest reduction in solar share, whereas increases in dish area or operating temperature mainly raise the solar contribution with more limited economic benefit. The findings demonstrate that optimal Solar-MGT performance arises from balanced combinations of design parameters rather than extreme values. The results highlight the importance of integrated, year-round techno-economic modelling for identifying realistic design pathways and guiding future Solar-MGT deployment.

Integrating sufficiency into climate neutrality scenarios: From socio-technical context scenarios to energy system optimisation models
abstract: Climate neutrality scenarios demonstrate energy transition pathways with varying foci. Most existing scenarios prioritise technology-based mitigation options, partly due to the technology focus of existing models. The approach presented in this paper widens the solution space by employing a comprehensive mix of methods that also considers the energy service demand side. A tool chain for developing and evaluating socio-technical context scenarios based on the cross-impact-balance (CIB) method, the simulation model Pathway Explorer (PWE) and the energy system optimisation tool PyPSA are applied. Two of the resulting six climate neutrality scenarios for Germany are green-growth-oriented, and four are sufficiency-oriented with varying characteristics. Scenarios combining fast technological development with sufficiency aspects reducing energy service demand perform best in terms of emission reductions and costs. A comparison with existing climate neutrality scenarios shows that including sufficiency eases pressure on other strategies such as renewable energy generation or imports. Although not all components of the narratives can be translated into quantitative model parameters, the combination of existing tools is promising and opens up solution spaces. However, improvements are needed: demand-side modelling techniques across sectors and land-use conflicts must be better represented.

Effects of methane addition on soot formation characteristics in ammonia–air coflow flames
abstract: Ammonia offers the advantage of being carbon-free; however, its poor reactivity calls for co-firing with hydrocarbons, which improves reactivity but inevitably triggers soot formation. The mechanism of soot activation in ammonia-dominated environments remains poorly understood. This study investigates soot formation characteristics in ammonia/methane co-flow nonpremixed flames across the entire blending ratio range (0–100%) using a detailed sectional soot model. The results reveal a highly non-linear threshold effect: below 20% CH4, soot inception occurs but HACA surface growth is negligible, and OH oxidation dominates, leading to zero net soot accumulation. Once methane exceeds 20%, the HACA growth rate surges by several orders of magnitude, definitively overcoming OH oxidation and triggering exponential soot volume fraction (SVF) increase. The primary particle number density (Np) increases nearly linearly with methane content, whereas the average primary particle diameter (Dp) grows exponentially, demonstrating a clear decoupling between particle count and size. The exponential rise of SVF is therefore driven by rapid HACA mass addition rather than by an increase in particle number alone. Furthermore, as methane exceeds 40%, the global chemical mass fluxes approach saturation, but the soot morphology transitions from a compact droplet to an elongated wing shape. This morphological shift is governed by intense axial thermal stretching and increased upward velocity, confirming that the macroscopic shape transition is controlled by aerothermodynamic convection rather than by further chemical intensification. These findings suggest a kinetic “switch” for soot activation in ammonia flames and decouple the chemical growth from the physical morphological evolution.

title: Effects of synchronised remote work on office energy use: A three-year field study
abstract: : Remote work is increasingly recognised as an operational strategy with the potential to reduce office-level energy use. The key idea explored here is that, beyond the amount of remote work adopted, synchronising it across employees may enhance this potential. Synchronised schedules can create predictable low-occupancy days that allow non-essential services in large portions of the building to be reduced or switched off. Against this background, the study contributes field-based evidence on this organisational question under real operating conditions. The analysis is based on a three-year field study conducted in a fully electric office building in Cagliari, Italy, comparing three operational conditions: no remote work, unsynchronised remote work, and synchronised remote work on a designated day (Friday). High-resolution measurements of building electricity use, occupancy, and outdoor air temperature were analysed using multiple linear regression and climate normalisation. Results show that, in the analysed case, unsynchronised remote work was associated with a 29% reduction in normalised electricity use (95% CI: 25.3–32.6) compared with no remote work. Synchronised remote work was associated with a further reduction of 5.6% (95% CI: 0.7–12.0) relative to the unsynchronised arrangement. On the remote-work day, average savings reached 37.3% (95% CI: 24.4–49.6). Overall, the findings provide field-based evidence that, within the boundary conditions of the analysed case, synchronising remote work is associated with lower office-level electricity use and that schedule coordination can serve as an operational lever to enhance its energy-saving effectiveness.

abstract: Molten Carbonate Electrolysis enables high-temperature co-electrolysis of CO 2 and H 2 O to syngas, offering an attractive route for carbon utilization and flexible power-to-X operation under variable renewable electricity. However, physics-based performance models often require extensive parameterization and are not readily applicable for rapid screening, control-oriented prediction, or operating-point optimization. In this work, compact feedforward artificial neural networks are developed as fast surrogate models to predict MCE cell voltage from operating conditions using literature datasets. Four single-hidden-layer ANN models were trained in MATLAB using Levenberg-Marquardt learning with Bayesian regularization and dropout: (i) a temperature-current density model with a 2-3-1 architecture, (ii) a fuel-side composition model with a 5-5-1 architecture, (iii) an oxidant-side composition model with a 4-4-1 architecture, and (iv) a combined thermal-flow model with a 9-5-1 architecture, where the notation denotes input-hidden-output neurons. The proposed models reproduce experimental polarization behavior with unseen test-set relative errors on the order of 0.3-0.4% and capture key nonlinear dependencies across the investigated operating ranges. Finally, the combined 9-5-1 ANN surrogate is embedded in a constrained optimization workflow to identify operating conditions that minimize cell voltage at fixed current density while improving electrochemical efficiency, yielding ANN-derived optimal thermal-flow parameters.

Evaluating the impacts of coordination for cascaded hydropower plants on the Mid-Columbia
abstract: The Mid-Columbia region in the U.S. Pacific Northwest includes seven large, cascaded hydropower plants with a combined nameplate capacity of nearly 14 GW. These plants have several different operators, and there is currently limited coordination among the operators. We develop a detailed model of the Mid-Columbia system that captures both river flow constraints and power system operations. We then place this detailed model within a production cost model of a 2030 system of the Western Interconnection to evaluate how coordination of the Mid-Columbia hydropower plants might impact operations throughout the interconnection. We find that coordination of the Mid-Columbia plants leads to more generation from the Mid-Columbia plants and increased revenues for the Mid-Columbia operators. This benefit is achieved primarily through better utilization of the storage reservoirs and decreased spill through the cascade. We also evaluate the impacts of look-ahead on production costs and find that longer look-ahead values result in lower system-wide production costs.

How far is the European Union from a decarbonised building stock?
abstract: ABSTRACT With the building sector accounting for 30% of global emissions (40% with embodied emissions), this study assesses the progress of the European Union (EU) towards a decarbonised building stock. In line with national Nearly Zero-Energy Building (NZEB) requirements, energy performance and renewable integration are evaluated. Significant gaps are found in both areas. Residential buildings require the most substantial improvements in energy performance – a decline of 3 % per year – while non-residential buildings need to maintain current upgrading rates of 2.7 % per year. Although higher compliance is observed regarding renewable energy use as compared with energy performance, generation must increase by 2.8%/year to cover the energy demand in 2050. The study highlights the need to harmonise indicators, enhance data quality, revise national thresholds, and accelerate renovation rates to achieve widespread energy savings in the existing building stock. Additionally, it emphasises the importance of addressing both operational and embodied emissions, incorporating circularity strategies and Life Cycle Assessment to inform balanced decision-making. These findings offer valuable insights for policymakers to define coherent requirements and roadmaps for climate neutrality. A holistic approach—encompassing energy efficiency, behavioural change, low-carbon materials and clean energy adoption—is essential to the EU’s transition towards a decarbonised building environment, with affordable and sustainable living spaces.

Dynamic modeling and multi-unit thermal coupling analysis of a pressurized water reactor based common-header steam supply system under extreme scenarios
abstract: With the large-scale grid integration of renewable energy, the demand for non-baseload operation of nuclear power plants has become increasingly prominent. Maintaining the reactor near nominal operating conditions while achieving power tracking through co-generation is beneficial for enhancing energy efficiency, reactor safety and power supply flexibility. However, for steam supply in the petrochemical sector, extreme load variations pose a triple challenge and trade-off between steam production reliability, reactor safety, and power tracking stability. This study investigates a common-header nuclear steam supply system based on two pressurized water reactors. A high-fidelity dynamic model comprising 20,869 equations was developed and validated using the Modelica language. Under a coordinated control mode, the dynamic characteristics of the system were simulated and evaluated under sharp steps in electrical and thermal loads. The results indicate that the common-header configuration effectively decouples the industrial steam supply from electrical transients, keeping thermal load deviations within 0.5 MW during 30% abrupt electrical fluctuations. Furthermore, symmetric load adjustments reach steady-state in approximately 600 s, significantly faster than the 2400 s required for asymmetric scenarios. During sudden thermal load losses, a dual-unit synchronized compensation strategy reduces electrical power overshoot by 4.93% to 10.63% compared to single-unit modes. Such insights reveal the coordinated mechanism of multi-unit thermo-electric coupling, providing theoretical guidance and modeling references for the design and flexible operation of PWR-based high-temperature steam supply systems.

abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy into power systems, the electrolytic aluminum load (EAL), as an energy-intensive industrial consumer, exhibits substantial regulation potential and can function as a key flexible resource for grid interaction. In this study, we aimed to characterize the heterogeneous regulation capabilities of the EAL across its three core production processes—electrolysis, feeding, and aluminum tapping—and to enable coordinated dispatch between distribution-side flexible resources and the transmission system under dual uncertainties stemming from captive wind power fluctuations and peak-shaving market price volatility. First, a refined multi-process regulation model is developed to systematically capture the differences among the three processes in their operational mechanisms, response speeds, and adjustable capacities. Second, to explicitly address uncertainties from both the transmission and distribution sides, a temporal conditional value-at-risk (CVaR)-based peak-shaving capacity correction model is proposed to dynamically revise the available peak-shaving capacity. Finally, the three production processes are allocated to the day-ahead, intra-day, and real-time scheduling stages according to their distinct regulation characteristics and are jointly coordinated with captive thermal power units, thereby facilitating wind power utilization and grid peak-shaving services. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances wind power utilization and overall economic performance while improving the reliability of EAL participation in grid operations.

title: Multifunctional triply periodic minimal surface-based metal hydride reactors: Topology optimization for enhanced thermal transport and hydrogen storage
abstract: Weight reduction and functional integration are key challenges in next-generation energy systems. Advances in additive manufacturing (AM) enable complex internal architectures that combine structural support, thermal management, and energy storage within a single component. For hydrogen applications, this design freedom is promising for metal hydride (MH) storage systems, where high volumetric capacity is limited by low gravimetric performance and heat-transfer-controlled charging. This study proposes a multifunctional MH container based on triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures, including Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond geometries. Two configurations were investigated: a baseline TPMS with balanced domains (50% MH/50% heat-transfer region) and an offset TPMS with increased MH fraction (75% MH/25% heat-transfer domain). The effects of phase redistribution on thermal behavior, mechanical integrity, and hydrogen charging were evaluated. AM feasibility was assessed using overhang-angle distribution and printable surface area. Diamond TPMS showed the best balance of structural stability, thermal performance, and manufacturability and was further refined using density-based topology optimization via the Method of Moving Asymptotes (MMA). The optimization maintained the 75/25 domain ratio and employed an objective function targeting improved thermal transport through optimized material distribution. The optimized Diamond TPMS reached hydrogen saturation near 4000 s, compared with approximately 4500 s for the Diamond normal configuration and 7000 s for the Diamond offset configuration, corresponding to charging-time reductions of approximately 11% and 43%, respectively. This study confirms that topology-optimized TPMS architectures can enhance heat-transfer efficiency and hydrogen charging performance without reducing MH volume.

title: A field test data-driven heat balance-informed bivariate coal consumption modeling method for flexible thermal power unit scheduling
Extreme surges in hydropower headrace channels: A unified explicit analytical solution enabling scenario-adaptive regulation
Full-process analysis of hybrid wind-wave systems: From resource assessment to power generation estimation
Effects of enhanced in-cylinder flow on knock reduction in a direct injection spark-ignition engine
Source-load fluctuation matching-based planning of Island hybrid energy systems with wave power integration
Impact assessment of decarbonization policies on CCS technology diffusion in power sector: An agent-based approach
Planning and deployment strategies of distributed energy systems for urban forms in the megacity: A case study of Beijing
Multi-objective optimization of double-H finned tube heat exchangers via CFD-DEM: Entropy generation, fouling, and erosion analysis
abstract: H-type finned tube heat exchangers are widely used in heat transfer process of dusty gas. Problems such as flow resistance, fouling and erosion are multiple constraints restricting the design of such heat exchangers. This study establishes a multi-objective optimization framework combining RSM, entropy weight method and NSGA-Ⅱ algorithm, and adopts the CFD-DEM coupled method to simulate a double H-type finned tube heat exchanger, aiming to balance its thermodynamic efficiency, erosion resistance and anti-deposition performance under gas-solid two-phase flow. Firstly, a quadratic polynomial response surface model was developed to quantitatively correlate five key parameters (tube spacing, fin width, fin fillet radius, gas velocity, particle diameter) with three critical performance indicators, namely total entropy generation (ΔSpro), erosion rate (verosion), and deposition rate (Rd). The effects of parameter coupling on entropy generation, fouling and erosion were analyzed in further detail, revealing clear trade-offs and synergistic effects between the parameters. The Pareto solution obtained via NSGA-II resulted in an optimized design that reduced total entropy generation from 0.005957 W/K to 0.005815 W/K, and the erosion rate from 45.28×10⁻¹² m/s to 37.76×10⁻¹² m/s, but the deposition rate increased from 13.14% to 15.05%. The comprehensive performance of the heat exchanger has been improved. This work provides an effective optimization method for the design of tube heat exchangers in gas-solid two-phase flow conditions.

title: Techno-economic analysis of an integrated system of anaerobic digestion and pyrolysis reactors with Kalina power cycle
abstract: Waste management challenges have intensified in recent decades due to population growth and industrialisation. Among the various waste management strategies, waste-to-energy technologies have shown considerable potential; however, each method presents limitations when implemented individually. In this context, the integration of multiple technologies can significantly enhance overall system performance. The integration of anaerobic digestion (AD) with pyrolysis (PY) has recently attracted increasing attention and has been investigated primarily through experimental studies. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive numerical model of this integrated system to improve process understanding and identify potential operational challenges. The system was further coupled with a Kalina cycle to enhance energy recovery and enable cogeneration. Following detailed modelling, the system was evaluated through energy, exergy, economic, and environmental (4E) analyses. The results indicated that the energy efficiency increased from 12.16% to 19.59% after integration with the Kalina cycle. The exergy efficiency of the integrated system was calculated to be 38.15% and increased further to 40.1% with the addition of a cooling subsystem. From an economic perspective, the fully integrated system demonstrated a payback period of 2.51 years. Environmentally, the system achieved specific CO 2 emissions of 0.3861 kg CO 2 /kWh. These findings, supported by the 4E assessment, contribute to the advancement of sustainable waste management and energy production, particularly in developing countries.

title: High-fidelity modeling of pressurized water reactor flow fields for data-driven applications
abstract: This work presents a high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and data-driven modeling framework for assembly-level flow characterization in a four-loop pressurized water reactor (PWR). A full lower-plenum and core-inlet domain was constructed using publicly available geometry and operating conditions, enabling transient simulations with pump-induced swirl boundary conditions. The results show that pump-induced cold-leg swirl and lower-plenum transport generate strongly heterogeneous assembly-wise inlet flow distributions, particularly near the lower core region, while axial resistance and mixing progressively homogenize the flow at higher elevations. These physics-informed datasets were subsequently used to evaluate machine learning (ML) applications for partial field reconstruction and short-term autoregressive prediction. A 3D convolution-based inpainting model successfully reconstructed missing assembly-level mass flow rates from partial observations, with errors concentrated in the highly turbulent base (bottom) layer and diminishing significantly in upper layers. Comparative analysis across multiple ML models demonstrates that spatially aware architectures, particularly ConvLSTM, significantly outperform sequence-based (LSTM) and operator-learning (DeepONet) approaches by effectively capturing coupled spatio-temporal dynamics. The study also highlights key challenges, including the sensitivity of inlet flow predictions to turbulence and mesh resolution, as well as the absence of full-scale experimental validation data. Despite these limitations, the results remain consistent with expected physical behavior. Overall, this work establishes high-fidelity CFD as a critical foundation for developing data-driven surrogates, sparse sensing strategies, and future multiphysics coupling frameworks, while outlining directions for scalable, interpretable, and multi-fidelity learning approaches in nuclear reactor modeling.

title: Economic mitigation strategy for the duck curve phenomenon: Revealing the effectiveness of green hydrogen
Energy optimization of cold storage driven by new energy: A coupled temperature control strategy integrating photovoltaics, energy storage, and grid electricity prices
Thermo-economic assessment of an optimized semi-continuous green hydrogen production process by aluminum-water splitting in aqueous NaOH stream
abstract: Finding new cost-effective sources of green hydrogen is a top priority today, given the rapid adoption of hydrogen as an energy vector with potential of reducing the carbon footprint. To this purpose, emerging technologies capable of simultaneously performing both CO2 capture and H2 generation strategically offers the possibility of integrating these two relevant energy-related economies. Alternatives to water electrolysis such as the use of metal by-products or wastes to generate hydrogen from water can also contribute to a faster and more cost-effective development of green hydrogen. In this context, the present work publishes a new technology aiming at generating green hydrogen by reacting aluminum with a CO2-capture lean stream in a paked-bed semi-continuous reactor. The implemented methodology combines experimental research, statistically designed, with process simulation for stablishing optimal operative conditions (Temperature, Flow and NaOH concentration), allowing performing a further thermo-economic assessment of the proposed technology. The major contribution to the process overall cost is the cost of the aluminum-based metallic bed, that can be lowered by considering cheaper aluminum sources like Al-turnings, therefore showing profitability insights facing the current market prices for green hydrogen.

title: A simplified effectiveness–NTU framework for early-stage design of industrial solar thermal networks derived from data-driven models

Churning power loss evaluation of wide-speed oil-immersed motor-pumps based on a multi-dimensional coupling model

Removal mechanism of sulfur compounds from Zhundong coal using supercritical carbon dioxide-cosolvent systems
Thermally coupled pumped thermal energy storage system for a renewable powered ammonia production: Performance assessment and optimal sizing
abstract: The paper investigates the ability of pumped thermal energy storage system, coupled with renewable energy generators, to meet the electrical and thermal demands of an ammonia production plant. A steady-state model of an industrial-scale Haber–Bosch process is first developed to quantify the electrical and thermal energy demands and to identify high-temperature waste heat streams suitable for recovery. A tailored pumped thermal energy storage configuration is then designed and simulated. The storage system performance is characterized through a parametric analysis with respect to the compression ratio and the relative sizing of the charging and discharging power ratings. The resulting performance maps are then embedded into an optimization model for sizing the renewable generation and storage subsystems while minimizing the total system cost. Results show that the optimal configuration is strongly influenced by the maximum allowed share of grid electricity: allowing a 10% grid contribution reduces the total cost by about 50% compared to the fully renewable case and leads to a cost-effective design in which the power rating of the pumped thermal energy storage system in discharging mode is equal to the nominal electrical demand of the ammonia plant, while the charging power is approximately 1.5 times the discharging power. Compared with a reference configuration without pumped thermal energy storage, the proposed system reduces total cost by approximately 3–10%, depending on grid contribution and design parameters.

title: Data-driven electricity–computing–thermal coordinated optimization for data centers with MDN-based scenario probability updating and ADMM with adaptive common degradation degree
abstract: Coordinated electricity–computing–thermal (ECT) operation of data centers (DCs) can effectively reduce operating cost and energy consumption. However, the dual uncertainty of computing-task demand and renewable generation poses major challenge to highly renewable and reliable DC power supply. To address this critical concern, this paper proposes an online ECT collaborative model for green-power-connected DC. First, the flexibility on the electricity, computing, and thermal sides is jointly exploited to realize the balance between power supply and computing demand. Second, a data driven joint uncertainty modeling method is developed, which combines Wasserstein generative adversarial networks with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) for joint scenario generation, and introduced convolutional neural network trained mixture density network (CNN-MDN) for online estimating the initial probability distribution of joint scenario generation while rolling optimization with observation vectors. Third, a bi-level distributionally robust optimization (DRO) framework is developed based on a novel alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with adaptive common degradation degree, enabling parallel solution of the DC and energy subsystems and yielding optimal decisions from both power consumption and economic perspectives. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively exploit multi-flexibility resources, and significantly improve the temporal matching between renewable generation and computing demand. Compared with the baseline case without flexibility, the fully flexibility resources coordinated case reduces the total cost by 29.9% and the total DC power consumption by 9.3%. These results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in simultaneously improving the economy, energy efficiency, and operational robustness of DC.

title: Low-temperature and high-voltage sodium metal batteries enabled by non-solvating additives
Characterization of wake interference between two broken-line-bladed vertical axis wind turbines: Potential to increase the total power of wind farms
Adaptive robust control application scheme for nonlinear Kaplan hydro-turbine regulation system: based on the intelligent optimization algorithm and H∞ theory
Dynamic response characteristics of a 150 kW-class automotive PEMFC system: Impact of reactant supply timing regulation
Experimental investigation and energetic and exergetic evaluations of newly designed photocathodes for solar hydrogen production system
abstract: In this study, a novel and efficient solar-to-hydrogen energy conversion system based on photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting is developed as a promising alternative within the evolving energy ecosystem where hydrogen serves as a sustainable fuel, a key feedstock, and an energy storage medium. Hydrogen production is experimentally investigated in a specifically designed PEC reactor for the dimensions of the photoelectrodes. The developed photocathodes are based on an unconventional brass substrate, on the surface of which photoresponsive layers such as Cu 2 O and ZnO naturally exist. TiO 2 doped with Ir and Mo, both individually and in a co-doped combination, is deposited on this surface via spin- and dip-coating methods. The photoelectrocatalysts are synthesized using the sol–gel method, and doping with Ir (1%, 3%, and 5%), Mo, and Ir–Mo combinations is employed to improve PEC performance. The photocathodes are evaluated through energy efficiency, exergy efficiency, applied bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE), and hydrogen yield. The highest hydrogen production rate of 59.98 μmol/cm 2 h is achieved with 1% Ir-doped TiO 2 deposited via dip coating, corresponding to energy, exergy, and ABPE efficiencies of 4.03%, 4.14%, and 0.49%, respectively. More importantly, the use of a non-traditional brass substrate leads to an unexpected observation, where an inversion in behavior is identified, which reveals the critical role of the substrate’s natural surface oxide layers and substrate-induced interfacial effects in PEC performance.

title: Enhancing the energy and environmental performance of third-generation district heating systems via wastewater heat integration
abstract: Third-generation district heating networks remain widespread across Europe and are typically designed for high supply temperatures, which limits the integration of renewable and low-temperature heat sources. This study investigates the potential of using treated wastewater as a heat source for high-temperature heat pumps integrated into an existing third-generation district heating network, using Zagreb as a case study. Two configurations are compared: a single-stage cycle with R600a, limited to supply temperatures up to 75 °C, and a cascade cycle with R290/R1233zd(E), covering the full range of network supply temperatures. The analysis is based on real hourly operational data from both the wastewater treatment plant and the district heating system during the heating season. Empirically derived temperature-demand relationships are additionally provided to enable preliminary assessments in other cities with similar infrastructure. The cascade configuration achieves an effective seasonal coefficient of performance of 2.44, covers 74.8% of the seasonal heating demand, and reduces primary energy consumption by 41.13% and CO2 emissions by 54.08% compared with the baseline. The single-stage configuration covers 60.5% of demand with an effective seasonal coefficient of performance of 1.61. A sensitivity analysis confirms that the cascade system maintains positive primary energy savings across virtually the entire range of European electricity mixes. The recovered heat from the cascade configuration is sufficient to continuously supply approximately 31 400 residential households. The study demonstrates that treated wastewater can be efficiently upgraded to the temperature levels required by third-generation district heating systems, with the cascade arrangement emerging as the preferred configuration for high-temperature networks.

Urban mitigation pathways for decarbonising infrastructure across sectors for sustainability
abstract: Urban infrastructure that covers multiple sectors provides an opportunity to support climate change mitigation. This research work provides a new approach for establishing urban mitigation pathways based on the territorial carbon dioxide emissions of urban infrastructure per sector and urban area. The approach is applied to 1200 urban areas worldwide with 4.73 GtCO 2 of total emissions from the energy, transport, residential, industry, waste, and agriculture sectors located within their boundaries in the reference year of 2022, averaging 2.32 tCO 2 per capita. In the baseline, total emissions could rise to 5.61 GtCO 2 in 2050. Alternatively, three scenarios represent pathways that are aligned with climate futures that limit global warming to 1.5 °C with no or limited overshoot. The alternative scenarios involve an emphasis on renewable energy, low demand, and shifting pathways and lead to 0.93 GtCO 2 , 0.62 GtCO 2 , or 0.97 GtCO 2 in 2050, respectively. Such urban areas as Tokyo, Shanghai, Los Angeles, and Guangzhou involve some of the largest reductions in one or more sectors between 2025 and 2035, reaching up to 30.56 MtCO 2 and 53.33 MtCO 2 of reductions in the energy and industry sectors, respectively. Simulated values based on 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations indicate a range of 0.57 – 1.05 GtCO 2 in 2050 for the total emissions in the alternative scenarios. The results indicate that the 1200 urban areas hold numerous possibilities for decarbonising urban infrastructure within and across multiple sectors, underscoring their roles for the effective mitigation of climate change.

title: Analysis of advanced tools usage benefits in organizing urban citizen energy communities with photovoltaic integration
Decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors: A hybrid electrification approach for low-carbon cement production
abstract: The decarbonization of energy-intensive industries, particularly the cement sector, is critical to achieving global climate targets. Cement production contributes approximately 7% of global CO 2 emissions, largely due to fossil fuel-powered clinker formation at around 1450 °C. Key challenges include heavy reliance on fossil-derived thermal energy, inefficient thermal energy utilization, and process emissions from calcination reactions. This research proposes an integrated decarbonization framework by electrification of the cement-making process and by incorporating green e-hydrogen, on-site wind and solar photovoltaic power generation, and a hybrid energy storage system comprising sodium-ion batteries and a molten carbonate fuel cell. Case studies across three European locations, with diverse renewable energy resources and climatic conditions demonstrate the broad applicability and effectiveness of the proposed system. The results show that a hybrid wind–solar setup could achieve up to a 45% emission reduction compared to the state-of-the-art, showing the system’s significant CO 2 mitigation potential. The technologies are scalable and adaptable beyond the case study locations offering a general solution to significantly reduce CO 2 emissions from cement production. Energy system costs of $252–285/MWh for wind-based systems, $247–272/MWh for hybrid solar–wind configurations, and $249–277/MWh for solar-based systems were achieved by electrifying the cement-making process.

title: Impact of hydro power site parameters on the Pelton injector using computational analysis
Component-level fault diagnosis in district heating networks by using a physics-based approach
abstract: A District Heating Network (DHN) is composed of several components that may be prone to faults; therefore, diagnostic tools are necessary to identify malfunctions that reduce system efficiency. This study presents a physics-based diagnostic tool for the detection and identification of faults in the key DHN components, namely, pumps, pipes, valves and heat exchangers. Fault detection involves locating the faulty component, whereas fault identification enables the estimation of fault signature as well as its magnitude. The proposed diagnostic tool relies on a physics-based model of the DHN. The governing equations include the variables (namely, health indices and valve opening) that are useful to assess the health state of each DHN component (i.e., healthy or faulty condition, and fault magnitude). The values of such variables are identified by means of an optimization algorithm. The DHN serving the Campus of the University of Parma (Italy) is used as a case study. Its operation is reproduced by means of a reliable data simulator in both healthy and faulty conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed diagnostic tool accurately evaluates the health state of all DHN components, i.e., both fault detection and fault signature are correctly identified. In addition, the difference between the actual and calculated fault magnitude is negligible in most cases, proving that the health state of each DHN component is always reliably estimated. Its reliability, computational efficiency, and robustness to noise make the diagnostic tool suitable for real-world applications.

title: Extended non-structural modeling and heat integration: Incorporating decoupled internal utility exchanger generation and conversion in energy systems

Upgrading solar thermal energy quality for industrial applications
abstract: ABSTRACT During 2024, 6 % of days had critical irradiance levels and 25 % had low irradiance levels. Furthermore, 52 % of global thermal energy consumption is attributed to low- and medium-temperature industrial sectors. This work maximizes the exergy potential of a coupled heat pump-solar thermal installation system (STI-HP). Using an advanced exergy analysis of STI-HP, avoidable exergy destruction is calculated. The proposed approach aims, firstly, to guarantee the heat load at the target process temperature year-round and to expand applications to low- and medium-temperature facilities using low-temperature solar thermal energy. A tomato paste processing plant operating from April 15th to October 15th is used as a case study. Four refrigerants were used to demonstrate the significant variation in exergy content. The thermodynamic cycle approach evaluates unavoidable/avoidable exergy destruction. Endogenous and exogenous destruction is calculated to determine the irreversibilities of each piece of equipment and their interaction. An analysis of economic indicators—LCOE (cost of energy), SPB (simple payback), and NPV (net present value)—was conducted to determine the system's profitability. The entire heat load was supplied at 155.6 °C for the 183 days of process operation. Ethanol was the best working fluid, with a = 70 °C, the highest COP HP of 4.64 ( = 74.4 %), and the lowest LCOE of 0.0818 USD/kWh. Compared to R141b ( = 70 °C), ethanol increased COP by 10.7 % and the exergy efficiency by 5 %.Upgrading quality of energy expands the application range to include low- and medium-temperature industrial sectors.

title: Integrating an enhanced diversification metric into energy system models to assess the security and resilience of renewable-based energy systems towards carbon neutrality
abstract: Energy systems are changing as a result of the transition to renewable energy from fossil fuels and the increased deployment and integration of fluctuating renewable energy sources. However, global supply chain challenges, energy crises, and geopolitical conflicts have underlined the need for not only reducing carbon emissions and optimising costs in energy systems but also ensuring energy security and resilience. This adds new dimensions to energy system modelling and to the evaluation of energy system scenarios as an integral part of energy strategy and energy policy development. This study reviews existing energy security and resilience indicators and proposes a decentralisation adjusted diversity index approach for assessing the diversity of energy systems. The proposed diversity index method can be applied alongside different energy system modelling frameworks and can be applied ex post to modelling outputs, as demonstrated by its use with EnergyPLAN and OSeMOSYS for two different national cases, Denmark and Greece. Both cases highlight energy systems transitioning from fossil fuel-based energy systems towards 100% renewable energy systems. Hence the study uses the decentralisation adjusted diversity index to evaluate how the dynamics of energy system diversity changes with the transition to variable renewable energy resources. The phase-out of fossil fuels reduces traditional energy fuel type diversity; however, this is offset by the implementation of geographically dispersed renewable energy sources. This results in an overall increased energy diversity index value for renewable energy systems and thereby increased energy system security and resilience.

Attitudes toward climate change to demand-driven energy mitigation: A machine-learning approach
abstract: Promoting mitigation behaviors among the public is a fundamental step in addressing climate change, yet such efforts have achieved uneven success across demographic groups. This paper surveys the literature on the relationship between personal attitudes toward climate change and mitigation behaviors, with a particular focus on demand-side energy consumption reductions. An interpretative framework for understanding the key drivers of and barriers to common mitigation strategies is provided. Applying a machine-learning approach to survey data from 23 European countries to disentangle the relative importance of attitudinal predictors, the analysis finds that perceived personal responsibility for climate change is the single most powerful predictor of energy-conscious behavior. This paper thus offers a useful guide to understanding successful approaches to incentivizing climate-friendly action within this regional context.

Techno-economic analysis of Allam-cycle systems integrating Air Separation Unit-derived nitrogen for power generation
abstract: Directly fired supercritical CO 2 (sCO 2 ) power cycles have attracted growing attention for their potential to deliver high efficiency with inherent CO 2 capture. Among them, the Allam cycle stands out for its advanced development stage but remains limited by the high auxiliary demand of the Air Separation Unit (ASU). This work investigates the techno-economic potential of utilizing the ASU’s nitrogen byproduct as a secondary working fluid for additional power generation. A coupled MATLAB-Thermoflex framework was developed to model both the ASU and an Allam-based power block, incorporating thermal integration and oxygen supply constraints. The proposed configuration includes an open-Brayton N 2 expansion train integrated to enhance net power output without altering CO 2 recirculation. Monte Carlo analysis was applied to quantify uncertainty in component cost correlations and derive percentile-based capital expenditure (CAPEX). Results show that nitrogen integration increases net power output by 16.6% with only a 0.9% rise in total CAPEX, reducing the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) by up to 8.6% under adverse natural gas price conditions. The recuperator remains the main cost driver, representing 54.4% of the power-block investment. Although the integration yields clear thermodynamic and economic benefits, the system remains below break-even (Profitability Index, PI < 1) under current cost assumptions, indicating that further CAPEX reductions or policy support would be required for commercial feasibility.

title: A gray-box AEKF-based model for structural electricity demand forecasting in Mexico (2019–2027): Under real and nominal GDP
abstract: : Forecasting the electricity demand of a developing country plays a crucial role in its socioeconomic sustainability and feedback loops. Focusing on the Mexican case, this paper presents a novel gray-box mathematical model fed with population, average national temperature, and gross domestic product parameters, coupled with the Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (AEKF) method for recursive coefficient adjustment and the determination of average daily electricity demand. The model was trained during the period 2019–2023 and validated with out-of-sample data from 2024–2025. A key empirical finding was that when evaluating the model using real GDP in the validation phase, the prediction underestimates the amount of energy; however, using nominal GDP showed a significantly better fit, resulting in a mean error of only 0.1033 GW and an RMSE of ±1.425 GW with respect to the 7-day centered moving average of the measured data. This suggests that, in Mexico, aggregate electricity demand may be more sensitive to immediate liquid assets (M1) and expansions in nominal purchasing power rather than in indexed real production. Furthermore, variations in average temperature severely impact grid stress due to the pursuit of thermal comfort, demonstrating that a deviation above of just 2 °C above the historical average can lead to capacity-constraining conditions in the system. Consequently, projections for the 2026-2027 period anticipate critical conditions for the electricity grid if extreme temperature profiles like those observed in the last seven years occur.

title: Simulation investigation and mechanism analysis on the performance of a novel tab-nozzle ejector
A novel integrated system for decarbonizing coal chemical industrial parks: A comprehensive study on thermodynamic, economic, and environmental performance
Temperature uniformity enhancement in porous radiant burner ceramic using alumina spheres in the preheating zone
Improving safety, efficiency and power quality of grid-connected photovoltaic microgrid energy systems through advanced inverter structures and enhanced modulation strategies
abstract: Improving safety and energy efficiency in grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) microgrid energy systems requires effective coordination between inverter topology and modulation strategy. This paper presents a system-level evaluation of a proposed New Ten-Switch Inverter (NTSI) and an enhanced PWM strategy for the Hybrid-Leg Inverter (HLI), together with conventional transformerless inverter configurations and representative solutions reported in the literature, operating under identical grid-connected conditions. The results show that conventional configurations can produce leakage currents exceeding 300 mA at a DC-link voltage of 750 V, violating international safety limits. At the same operating condition, the proposed solutions reduce leakage current by 86% and common mode voltage (CMV) by 47.6% compared with the conventional configuration. In addition, the proposed solutions reduce leakage current to below 50 mA and significantly attenuate spectral components across fundamental and switching-frequency ranges. When the DC-link voltage increases to 1500 V, the conventional system exhibits severe leakage-current increase (3326 mA) and increased harmonic distortion (9.6%), whereas the proposed approaches maintain leakage current below 75 mA and total harmonic distortion below 2.2%, ensuring compliance with safety and grid quality requirements. At this voltage level, leakage-current reduction exceeds 97.9% relative to the conventional configuration and CMV reduction is 77.8%. The proposed solutions are comprehensively validated through both simulation and experimental investigations over a wide range of DC-link voltages, demonstrating consistent improvements in CMV, leakage current, and power quality. The comparative analysis further shows that leakage-current reduction and efficiency are closely coupled. While some configurations achieve strong suppression at the expense of higher losses, others provide a more balanced trade-off between safety, harmonic quality, and energy efficiency. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed NTSI and enhanced PWM strategy provide a balanced trade-off between safety, efficiency, power quality, and hardware complexity, while comprehensive comparison with representative transformerless inverter topologies confirms their practical advantages for grid-connected PV microgrid applications.

Advancing the spatial assessment of low-temperature heat sources: a multi-criteria decision-making framework applied to hydroelectric power stations in three Bavarian administrative districts
abstract: Low-temperature heat sources offer a promising yet underutilised solution for the heating transition, especially as a replacement for the fossil fuels currently used to heat buildings. This study enhances the methodology for assessing the use of such sources, defining a multi-criteria decision-making framework including spatial and regulatory parameters to systematically prioritise potential low-temperature heat source sites. It takes a two-step approach, first developing an expert-validated model using the Analytical Hierarchy Process, with criteria derived from three low-temperature heat source types (river thermal energy, industrial excess heat, and general low-temperature heat sources); and then applying this model to three Bavarian case studies, focusing on hydroelectric power stations. Results show that heat demand, source availability, protected areas, and distance between source and demand are the prime influencing criteria, with heat demand the dominating factor. The study primarily assesses geographical potential, classifying sites by suitability (A–C) and evaluating the robustness of the results through sensitivity analyses. The latter reveals that only 8–24 % of sites remain feasible under ambitious building energy retrofitting pathways, with buffers to protected areas greatly impacting feasibility. Regional variability across the case studies demonstrates the framework’s transferability. The methodology gives municipalities a data-driven tool bridging the gap between theoretical potential and practical implementation in their mandatory heating transition plans for achieving climate neutrality.

Integrated multigeneration system utilizing industrial gas engine waste heat for power, oxygen, hydrogen generation, and process heat supply: A thermodynamic, exergo-economic, and environmental analysis
abstract: Integrating waste heat recovery units into industrial energy infrastructure provides a sustainable solution by reducing reliance on fossil fuels and improving substantial plant efficiency. Recent studies have addressed this issue using Brayton, Rankine, organic Rankine, thermoelectric, and electrolysis-assisted waste heat recovery systems for power, heat, hydrogen, or other useful outputs. However, many configurations recover exhaust gas and jacket water heat separately, focus mainly on electricity, and provide limited source-to-sink matching for industrial steam, process heat, oxygen demand, cost, and environmental performance. This study proposes a source-to-sink matched multigeneration system for a 10 MW Wärtsilä 20V34SG gas engine, where each waste heat stream is directed to the most suitable conversion pathway to reduce irreversibility and improve usefulness. High-temperature exhaust gas is cascaded through a helium Brayton cycle, a steam Rankine cycle, and a thermoelectric generator, while jacket-water heat drives an organic Rankine cycle that supports PEM electrolysis for steam generation. Hydrogen is treated as an internal energy carrier rather than an exported product. A MATLAB-based framework evaluates the system through thermodynamic, exergo-economic, environmental, sustainability, parametric, and uncertainty analyses. Under baseline conditions, the system delivers 2527.3 kW power, 2231.3 kW heating, 0.30 ton/h steam, and 56.77 kg/h oxygen, with 7.15 kg/h hydrogen generation. Energy and exergy efficiencies reach 28.37% and 27.67%, while annual mean CO 2 reduction is 25,461 ton (95% uncertainty interval: 21,655–29,690 ton/year). Collectively, these advancements contribute to cleaner production by improving resource and energy utilization efficiency, reducing environmental emissions and thermodynamic irreversibilities.

A preference-aware reinforcement learning framework for cost-effective and comfort-driven coordinated building energy management
abstract: Building energy consumption accounts for up to 40% of global energy use, contributing substantially to greenhouse gas emissions. Although demand-side management (DSM) and intelligent control systems have been extensively studied for residential buildings, smart buildings still face critical challenges due to their complex energy consumption profiles and lack of flexible, multi-energy management frameworks. This paper presents a novel multi-objective coordinated energy management system (EMS) that integrates a preference-aware reinforcement-learning framework to balance energy cost and indoor thermal comfort by dynamically coordinating multiple building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), energy storage systems (ESS), and hydrogen storage tanks (HST). To support day-ahead operation under uncertain renewable generation, the proposed EMS incorporates an AI-based extreme learning machine (ELM) model enhanced by a historical data correlation evaluation (HDCE) method, which improves the accuracy of short-term photovoltaic (PV) generation predictions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework can achieve approximately 13.4% energy cost reduction while maintaining nearly negligible user discomfort. In addition, the integrated PV forecasting module achieves a prediction error of 3.33%, which provides reliable renewable input for the coordinated EMS.

title: Thermal performance of an asphalt solar collector coupled to a water-source heat pump for domestic hot water: A system simulation
abstract: Electrification is increasing the use of heat pumps for domestic hot water (DHW), but their performance remains strongly dependent on source temperature. This study evaluates whether an asphalt solar collector (ASC) integrated into a 600 m 2 parking area can provide seasonal source-side preheating for a water-source heat pump in Kaunas, Lithuania (54.9°N). An hourly model was run for 2015–2024 using ERA5 meteorological data and measured DHW demand. Building and vehicle shadows were represented through clipped polygon unions, collector heat transfer and hydraulics through flow-regime-specific correlations, and heat-pump capacity and electricity use through a manufacturer-based EN 14511 performance map that included operating limits, cycling, backup heating, standby demand and hydraulic auxiliaries. Under fixed-flow control, the shaded collector delivered 25.06 kWh m -2 yr -1 and increased the heat-pump seasonal coefficient of performance from 3.58 to 4.01. After collector pumping was included, the system seasonal performance factor was 3.92 and net electricity use fell by 8.66%. Variable-flow strategies increased gross heat collection by 4.6–4.7%, but reduced net electricity savings to 6.60–7.04% because of higher pumping demand. Across collector areas of 300–900 m 2 and storage volumes of 2.5–10 m 3 , the maximum electricity-saving ratio was 9.80%. Meaningful collection occurred mainly from April to October, and neither economic nor carbon payback was achieved within the assumed 25-year service life. The system should therefore be regarded as a seasonal efficiency measure rather than a year-round heat source, with stronger prospects in sunnier, less shaded locations or projects that can realise additional pavement-related benefits.

title: Verified energy efficiency and renewable microgrid planning for remote educational infrastructure: A Pelee Island case study
abstract: This study presents an integrated modeling and optimization framework for a renewable microgrid designed to supply a proposed middle school on Pelee Island, Canada, a grid-constrained island relying on an aging underwater power cable. A detailed building energy model developed in eQUEST, incorporating site-specific climate data, occupancy schedules, and HVAC configuration, establishes an hourly electricity demand profile totaling 152.8 MWh/year. Space heating dominates end-use consumption at 40%, with peak demand reaching 16.82 MWh in January. Techno-economic optimization identifies an optimal hybrid configuration consisting of a 50-kW photovoltaic array, two 20 kW wind turbines, a 160 kW biogenerator, and a 221-kWh battery bank with a 146-kW converter. Operating under a cost-based dispatch strategy, the system produces 247,658 kWh/year with zero unmet load, achieving a cost of energy (COE) of $0.269/kWh and a net present cost (NPC) of $604,702 over the project lifetime, with a payback period of 8.7 years. Wind, photovoltaic, and biogenerator sources contribute 23.6%, 27.5%, and 48.9% of total generation, respectively. System performance is verified using an IPMVP-informed, weather-normalized baseline incorporating weekday and weekend regression models at a balance temperature of 23°C, yielding R2 values of 0.76 and 0.71, respectively. Two energy conservation measures (ECMs) are evaluated: an enthalpy wheel recovering 35,216 kWh/year in heating energy and an electric preheater delivering 6,035 kWh/year in auxiliary savings. The biogenerator operates for 1,482 hours/year, consuming 21.5 tonnes of biomass fuel, while the wind turbines achieve a capacity factor of 38.9%, reflecting strong year-round resource utilization at the site.

title: Beyond power-to-hydrogen: An integrated hexageneration platform for renewable surplus valorization
abstract: : The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources is leading to growing amounts of surplus electricity that cannot be directly integrated into power systems, particularly in isolated island grids with limited flexibility. While renewable surplus electricity is commonly converted into hydrogen, its simultaneous transformation into multiple strategic products has received considerably less attention. This study proposes an integrated hexageneration platform for the comprehensive valorization of renewable surplus electricity using the annual surplus generated after the integration of the Chira–Soria Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) system into the Gran Canaria electricity network. The proposed platform integrates Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis, reverse osmosis desalination, Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) and Haber–Bosch synthesis to simultaneously produce hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, green ammonia and desalinated water. Mass and energy balances were integrated with economic and environmental assessments to evaluate the overall performance of the proposed system. The available renewable surplus of 1,811,482.96 MWh·year -1 enables the annual production of 28,977.88 t of hydrogen, 231,823.04 t of oxygen, 135,229.11 t of nitrogen, 164,207.99 t of green ammonia and 261,061.08 m 3 of desalinated water. The economic assessment indicates that product diversification substantially increases the value of renewable surplus utilization compared with conventional hydrogen-only pathways, while simultaneously creating opportunities for industrial gas production, maritime decarbonization, fertilizer manufacture and freshwater supply. Depending on the commercialization strategy adopted, the proposed system may generate annual revenues exceeding 200 M€·year -1 while simultaneously improving renewable resource utilization. The proposed framework extends the conventional Power-to-Hydrogen concept towards an integrated renewable surplus valorization strategy, providing a scalable methodology for improving renewable resource utilization, economic diversification and energy security in isolated island energy systems.

CFD-based multi-objective optimization of operating conditions in a small-scale ORC radial-inflow turbine using response surface methodology
abstract: This study presents a CFD–RSM framework for constructing surrogate-based operating maps and optimizing the operating conditions of a manufactured small-scale radial-inflow turbine used in an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system. Unlike studies focused mainly on turbine redesign, the proposed approach addresses operating-point selection for an existing experimentally characterized turbine with fixed geometry and working fluid. Four operating variables are considered: rotational speed, inlet temperature, inlet pressure, and outlet pressure, with admissible ranges constrained by the coupled operation of the feed pump, condenser, and turbine. A design of experiments with 355 operating points is generated using Latin Hypercube Sampling and evaluated using steady-state three-dimensional CFD simulations with real-gas thermophysical properties. Polynomial response surface models are then fitted to predict turbine isentropic efficiency and power output across the admissible operating range. The results show that a first-order response surface provides the most robust prediction, with validation errors below 5% against independent CFD simulations. The surrogate model is subsequently used for single- and multi-objective optimization. The optimized operating points reveal a clear trade-off between efficiency and power output: the maximum-efficiency and maximum-power conditions do not coincide, while the nominal design condition remains close to the favorable Pareto-optimal region. The resulting operating map enables rapid evaluation of candidate operating points and provides a transferable decision-support methodology for reducing trial-and-error testing and supporting experimental planning and operation of small-scale ORC systems.

Experimental study on the heat transfer and flame scale characteristics of inclined tunnel fires under longitudinal ventilation
abstract: The dynamic behavior of leaked liquid fuel fires in inclined tunnels severely threatens structural safety and complicates personnel evacuation, while their combustion and smoke diffusion characteristics are subjected to the significant coupling effects of tunnel slope and longitudinal ventilation velocity. To explore the mass loss rate and heat feedback mechanism of such fires in longitudinally ventilated inclined tunnels, experiments were performed with n-Heptane fires under different tunnel slopes and longitudinal ventilation velocities of 0.5 to 3.0 m/s. The results show the different mass loss rate variation patterns of fuel fires in the tunnel inclination direction, while the longitudinal ventilation velocity significantly alters the flame combustion characteristics. Meanwhile, tunnel slope significantly modifies the smoke transport mode by altering the flow field pressure distribution, which redistributes the relative contributions of convective, radiative, and conductive heat feedback. Based on analyses of mass loss rate, smoke transport, and heat feedback redistribution, empirical correlations are established for flame-scale parameters at reduced scales herein. This study provides reference data and physical insights into the coupling effect of longitudinal ventilation velocity and tunnel slope in reduced-scale tunnel fires, thus supporting future large-scale experiments and model development.

A heat exchanger network retrofit method for non-continuous processes based on reinforcement learning
abstract: Non-continuous industrial processes exhibit irregular operating behaviour, characterised by frequent transitions and poorly defined operating regimes. To facilitate systematic analysis and optimisation, such processes are therefore commonly approximated as a set of representative discrete operating states. This study proposes an integrated reinforcement learning framework for heat exchanger network retrofitting under multiple operation states of non-continuous process. The reinforcement learning framework then optimises exchanger areas and network structure while respecting practical retrofit constraints. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that rely on surrogate models or direct prediction of optimal designs, the proposed framework embeds learning within the optimisation process to adaptively explore retrofit decisions under non-continuous operation. Compared with traditional deterministic optimisation algorithms that require explicit enumeration of all structural constraints and may become infeasible for complex networks, the reinforcement learning approach employs trial-and-error learning on simplified models with fixed exchanger areas, enabling robust optimisation of the overall retrofit problem. Case study results show that the proposed approach reproduces optimisation trends comparable to those obtained using the full dataset and achieves a reduction in total annual cost, with exchanger reassignment and minor retrofit modifications alone delivering savings of approximately $300,000–500,000 and permitting additional heat exchangers increasing the benefit to over $1,000,000.

title: Experimental and numerical investigations of the combustion characteristics and global reaction pathways of fuel NO in the methane/ammonia flame
abstract: The blending combustion of methane and ammonia is a promising strategy that can effectively address the inherent disadvantages of ammonia, such as ignition difficulty, low reactivity, and combustion instability. However, the high NO emission is still a considerable barrier in ammonia utilization. This study utilized the N-labeled chemical kinetic mechanism to distinguish between fuel and thermal NO, demonstrating the predominance of fuel NO in the CH4/NH3 swirling flame. The Global Pathway Analysis method was adopted to investigate the pathways governing the formation and consumption of the fuel NO at various equivalence ratios, ammonia blending ratios, and inlet velocities. The results indicated that the fuel NO emissions reached peaks under ER = 0.8 and RNH3 = 40% at different equivalence ratios and ammonia blending ratios, respectively. Increasing the inlet velocity led to the competition of thermal power and residence time, resulting in the lowest fuel NO emission under V = 220 cm/s. The radicals HNO and NH are critical intermediates to produce the fuel NO via the pathways of NH3 --> NH2 --> HNO --> NO and NH3 --> NH2 --> NH --> HNO --> NO. The dominance of the direct oxidation pathway through HNO within the chamber reduces as the equivalence ratio rises, while increases at high ammonia blending ratio and inlet velocity.
